body.title: problem: add old-to-new URL redirects to Git-over-SSH
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested on a next instance)

### About your usage of Forgejo

I often change naming conventions and just need to rename stuff. Git repos and orgs are no difference. Forgejo is a perfect replacement for most of the things, with just one thing missing for me: **SSH repo redirects** on repo/org name changes.

### Problem description

GitHub allows me to rename a repo and sets up redirect to old repo. Now, Forgejo actually supports that too, but **only for HTTPS**, not for SSH. I would like it to also work for Git-over-SSH clones, which take up a majority of my deployment scenarios. The scenario is simple:
- User creates a new organisation and/or new repo.
- User clones this new repo using SSH URL (Git-over-SSH).
- User renames the organization or repo or both at the same time.
- Fetch/push now fails until I change the URL. This can be really hard to trace down as there can be many deployments of the same repo in our company. 

Now, Forgejo could just redirect as it does in Git-over-HTTPS, inform the user about the repo/org name change and potentially log the redirect so admin can trace this occurence and fix it without it breaking in the meantime. 

Of course, if the repo/org name has been shadowed by a new one, the redirect shouldn't happen at all, as GitHub or similar services do the same.

### Potential workarounds

I believe the fix is fairly simple, just add a few checks to `routers/private/serv.go` and a hook to `cmd/serv.go` which fires **only when the redirect happened** (`strings.EqualFold(results.OwnerName, username` and simillar `if` for the repo itself) and:
- Informs the client by sending a message like: `this repository has moved to %s/%s.\nplease update your remote: git remote set-url origin %s\n`
- Logs the redirect so an admin can trace it or SIEM can evaluate that it happened.

### Forgejo Version

v17.0.2, but tested also on `1a13355` (Next, commit from `2026-11-20`) and it still behaves the same.

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

I don't think this is relevant, but:
Forgejo v17.0.2
Git: several clients: 2.56.1 on Fedora 44, 2.47.3 on Debian 13

### Solutions

*Accepted solutions to address this problem will go here*

body.title: problem: ucode-lang (ucode) is detected as unrealscript
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Unknown, I can't try it for some reason (please explain)

### About your usage of Forgejo

I use Forgejo through codeberg.org and do not have a Forgejo instance to test with, however searching Forgejo issues and pull requests does not match 'unrealscript' or 'ucode'. GitHub also does not handle this correctly as [ucode-lang](https://github.com/ucode-lang/ucode) is a fairly niche ECMAScript-like language, primarily used by [OpenWrt](https://openwrt.org) that happens to use the typically uses same file extension (`.uc`) as unrealscript (although `ucode` doesn't really care about the extension).

For a sample repo with which one can see the issue see: https://codeberg.org/danielfdickinson/uwatchcat

### Problem description

I have a repo https://codeberg.org/danielfdickinson/uwatchcat for which the main code is written in [ucode](https://github.com/ucode-lang/ucode) aka `ucode-lang`. The ucode scripts are detected and reported as `UnrealScript`

### Potential workarounds

_No response_

### Forgejo Version

I think 17 with modifications (https://codeberg.org/Codeberg-Infrastructure/forgejo)

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

Although this occurs with Codeberg, when I was running my own Forgejo instance  (15 then 16) I noticed the same behaviour. (I gave up on self-hosting due to LLM abusive crawlers).

### Solutions

body.title: problem: forgejo-cli actions register: --secret-stdin should be a boolean flag, not a string flag
body.body:
### Does your problem still exist on the latest Forgejo version?

Yes, the problem still exists (tested on a next instance)

### About your usage of Forgejo

I'm migrating off of Gitea to Forgejo and am figuring out runner registration using the CLI.

### Problem description

- I wanted to register a runner while piping its secret through stdin, without putting the secret in process arguments.
- On Forgejo 15.0.12 (LTS), --secret-stdin requires a string value, so I just used --secret-stdin=dummyto get it to work. I found the source [here](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/tag/v15.0.12/cmd/forgejo/actions.go#L71). It is the same for the latest branch. The actual secret value is piped in through std.in as you would expect and that functionality works fine.
- The assigned value (in this case "dummy") is completely ignored in the source code: SubcmdActionsRegister() declares a string flag, while readSecret() only checks whether it is set.

I expected --secret-stdin to work without a value being given to the argument - the actual secret comes from std.in and works fine.

Does it make sense to just change this to a BoolFlag so there is no need to pass a value here? The value is ignored anyway.

### Potential workarounds

I can just give a value and it works but it feels wrong.

### Forgejo Version

latest and on LTS 15.0.12 (which I tested)

### Other details about your environment (software names and versions)

I tested on On Forgejo 15.0.12 (LTS) - docker compose but the code is the same on the main branch.

Links:
- [On forgejo branch](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/src/branch/forgejo/cmd/forgejo/actions.go#L72) 



### Solutions
